subject: Error Message - Could not compute standard errors

messages.author: 894ba0144a04d3ae
messages.subject: Error Message - Could not compute standard errors
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am working on a pathway analysis of 3 continuous latent variables and one categorical outcome variable.
The following is my code:

model <- '
# latent variable definitions
  # exogenous variable
l1 =~ 1*CTQ_SA + CTQ_PA + CTQ_EA + CTQ_EN + CTQ_PN
  # endogenous variables
l2 =~ 1*ECR_av10 + ECR_anx10
l3 =~ 1*YSQ_DR + YSQ_IA + YSQ_OD

# regressions
l2 ~ l1
l3 ~ l2
RV ~ l3

# covariances
l1~~l1
l2~~l2
l3~~l3
RV~~RV '

fit<- sem(model, data=data, meanstructure = TRUE, ordered = c("RV"))

and I get the following warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
2: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic

This is the first time I am using R and also the first time I am doing a pathway analysis, so I'd appreciate any help or tips to resolve these issues!

messages.subject: Re: Error Message - Could not compute standard errors

messages.subject: Re: Error Message - Could not compute standard errors
parts:
Thank you for the quick response!
Do you have any suggestions what I could do to solve that problem?

mal...@malonequantitative.com schrieb am Samstag, 23. Januar 2021 um 15:15:46 UTC+1:
The problem is likely that I2 has only two indicators and no additional constraints. If the I2 -> I3 relation isn't strong enough to make up for it, the model may be empirically underidentified.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Error Message - Could not compute standard errors
parts:
If ECR_av10 and ECR_anx10 are on the same scale, it may be that this:

l2 =~ 1*ECR_av10 + 1*ECR_anx10

Will not be a bad mis-specification, and would probably fix the problem.
